title: Check 4b(i) ignores the provenance record's verdict/reason fields — a REFUTED record still backs a close
description: rk-tlwb schema/check divergence triage, 2026-08-12. schemas/provenance-record.v1.json makes 'verdict' a required const "VALID" and 'reason' a required non-blank string, because a record type whose sole purpose is to BACK a close has exactly one backing outcome (route (ii) refuses VALID-WITH-CORRECTION, so route (i) must not accept a weaker word) and an unexplained attestation is not auditable. src/reward/pma-backing.ts's provenanceDecision reads NEITHER field: it checks schema_version, claimId, role, author, and (since rk-io5l) claimSha256, then returns backed:true. So a hand-authored .rk/<name>.json carrying {"verdict":"REFUTED"} or no verdict at all still banks a proved-mod-audit close, provided the author is independent. 'rk reward attest' cannot emit one (src/reward/provenance-record.ts refuses), so the hole is only reachable by hand-writing a record — which is exactly what every campaign did for the two days before the producer existed. Fix: enforce verdict === 'VALID' and non-blank reason in provenanceDecision, with a red corpus fixture (record with verdict REFUTED => ERROR) and the gate-contracts Check 4b clause amended to list the two fields. Tier A: this is a validity semantic.

title: dogfood-2: linker gate (Gate 2) silently drops multi-line deps:/defs: values to empty, defeating DAG/unknown-id checks with zero warning
description:
Session: dogfood-2 (rk-bi4), campaign /home/tobiasosborne/Projects/rk-dogfood-1.

src/gates/snapshot.ts's parseFrontmatter is a strictly flat 'key: value' per-line
parser -- a line with no ':' (e.g. a YAML-list continuation line like "  - foo")
becomes a malformedLines entry, and the preceding "deps:" line's value stays "".
Only src/gates/defs.ts (Gate 1) reads fm.malformedLines and reports it; the
linker gate (Gate 2, src/gates/linker-parse.ts) never looks at malformedLines at
all.

Consequence, found live: dogfood-1's three argument shards were authored with
the natural-looking multi-line style:

    deps:
      - RD1-def-two-coloring
      - RD1-def-mono-triangle
      - RD1-def-bichromatic-angle

This is exactly what argument/README.md's own frontmatter table calls a
"`;`-list" field, and multi-line YAML lists are the conventional way to write a
list in frontmatter -- there is nothing in the README or the example shard that
warns single-line `;`-separated is required. Under this style, `deps` (and
`defs`, and `routes`) silently parse to the empty string. `rk check` reported
"checked linker: 3/3 lemma shards ... 0 errors, 0 warnings" for all three
shards even though two of them referenced other shards by id in this field --
the acyclic-graph, unknown-dep-id, and unknown-def-id checks (L4's "the
argument is an enforced acyclic graph") were validating nothing, with no
diagnostic of any kind.

Verified by perturbation (fixed in the campaign, not committed there in this
state): rewriting one shard's deps: with a genuinely unknown id in the correct
single-line syntax ("deps: RD1-lem-counting; RD1-nonexistent-id") produces the
expected "ERROR ... unknown dep 'RD1-nonexistent-id'"; the exact same bogus id
inserted as a second multi-line list item produces 0 errors, because the field
was already empty before the bogus id was ever considered.

This is a silent-skip class bug -- rk's own L2 says "a gate with no red fixture
does not exist... a silent skip is a bug, full stop," and this is precisely
that: the gate reports full coverage and zero findings while doing nothing.
Given L4/L5 frame the DAG enforcement as load-bearing for rigour, this may
warrant Tier A / L6 review per rk's own model policy (a wrong "0 errors" on a
broken graph is a validity-semantics bug, not a cosmetic one).

Suggested fix: either (a) have linker-parse.ts report fm.malformedLines the
same way defs.ts does, or (b) make parseFrontmatter (or a linker-specific
variant) understand multi-line YAML-style lists for deps:/defs:/routes:, or
(c) at minimum, add a fixture to the linker gate's red corpus that pins the
current (silently-empty) behavior so a future change can't make it worse
unnoticed, while the real fix (a or b) is scheduled.

title: dogfood-2: rk upgrade calls CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/PRD.md/HANDOFF.md 'safe overwrite candidates' but they hold campaign-filled slots a literal overwrite destroys
description:
Session: dogfood-2 (rk-bi4), campaign /home/tobiasosborne/Projects/rk-dogfood-1.

rk upgrade (1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 MISMATCH) prints per-file diff instructions and labels
CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, PRD.md, and HANDOFF.md as "rewritten-whole files (safe,
deliberate overwrite candidates -- diff and hand-merge)". Followed literally: stamped
a scratch preview with the current binary and diffed each named file against the
live campaign.

The label is misleading for a live campaign. All four files mix generated
template boilerplate with campaign-authored content that a scratch `rk init`
preview necessarily renders as placeholders:
  - CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/PRD.md: the goal statement, north-star contract (appears
    twice per file), and shard-id prefix (RUP- in the preview vs the campaign's
    real RD1-) all come back as literal placeholder text (`<placeholder north
    star>`) in the preview.
  - HANDOFF.md is worse: its preview version is a blank scaffold ("One-paragraph
    snapshot: what is established...") with none of the real State/Current
    work/Next steps content -- a naive `cp` would erase the campaign's actual
    session-state narrative entirely, the single field a returning session most
    needs.

"Diff and hand-merge" is the correct instruction and is what a careful user
does (I did, preserving all campaign slots) -- but calling these files "safe
overwrite candidates" in the same breath is contradictory framing that invites
exactly the wrong action from a less careful user, and the instructions never
explicitly flag WHICH parts of each file are campaign-owned vs template-owned.

Aggravating detail found in the same diff: the audit-trigger procedure text
in CLAUDE.md's rewritten §6 step 2 silently changes the session-close block
condition from "exceeds cadence" (>) to ">= cadence" -- a real governance-
semantics change, not just clarified prose, bundled inside a diff labeled a
safe overwrite candidate with no changelog or callout distinguishing wording
fixes from behavior changes. A user skimming the diff for "just clarity
improvements" could easily miss this off-by-one shift.

Suggested fix direction: either (a) rk upgrade's instructions should name the
specific campaign-owned slots in each rewritten-whole file (goal/north-star/
shard-prefix for CLAUDE.md-family, State/Current work/Next steps for
HANDOFF.md) so a user knows exactly what to preserve, or (b) stop calling
mixed-content files "safe overwrite candidates" and describe them as
"structural diff -- preserve your filled slots" instead. Separately, template
diffs that include a governance-semantics change (not just wording) should
say so explicitly.

title: dogfood-2: CLAUDE.md's read-order gate (§0, 'run fr board') is unenforced prose, unlike rk check which is wired into pre-commit
description:
Session: dogfood-2 (rk-bi4), campaign /home/tobiasosborne/Projects/rk-dogfood-1.

CLAUDE.md §0 ("Read-order gate") requires: "Before you add or change any
research content you must have read: PRD.md, this file, HANDOFF.md, and run
`fr board`." This session read PRD/CLAUDE/HANDOFF at the start but did not run
`fr board` until session close (while writing the audit-log entry) -- nothing
in the toolchain noticed or blocked on the omission. Contrast rk check, which
is wired into the git pre-commit hook and mechanically fires on every commit
attempt regardless of whether an agent remembers to run it.

Not a defect exactly -- fr board genuinely can't be a pre-commit gate the way
rk check is, since it's advisory/exploratory, not pass/fail -- but the
constitution presents it with the same imperative weight ("must have read...
and run") as the mechanically-enforced items, which sets an expectation the
tooling doesn't back up. An agent under time pressure has no signal that this
step was skipped.

Filing as a paper cut / design note rather than a bug: worth considering
whether `rk check` (or a lightweight session-start command) could emit an
advisory "fr board not run recently" note the way it already reports other
soft/advisory conditions, so the gap is visible rather than silent.

title: dogfood-2: audit cadence has no config-file source of truth; it's prose duplicated across CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and HANDOFF.md
description:
Session: dogfood-2 (rk-bi4), campaign /home/tobiasosborne/Projects/rk-dogfood-1.

Unlike linkerBrittlenessSoftCap, which has a real per-campaign home
(.rk/config.json's linkerBrittlenessSoftCap, referenced explicitly by
CLAUDE.md's brittleness-cap paragraph: "Tune it per campaign in `.rk/config`"),
the audit cadence (10 cycles by default) has no config-file field at all. It's
a number written into prose in three separate places: CLAUDE.md §6 step 2,
its AGENTS.md mirror (byte-identical by the file's own rule), and HANDOFF.md's
Audit cycle counter section ("Audit cadence: N cycles").

Lowering it for this dogfood session (10 -> 2, to actually exercise the
session-close block within a short run -- see rk-bi4 notes) required editing
all three by hand. Nothing checks the three copies stay in sync; a user who
edits only CLAUDE.md (the file they're most likely to think of first) leaves
HANDOFF.md's copy stale, and the two would silently disagree about what the
cadence actually is with no gate catching the drift (rk check doesn't parse
either file for this value).

Suggested fix: give audit cadence a .rk/config field (e.g.
`auditCadenceCycles`), have CLAUDE.md/HANDOFF.md's prose reference it by name
the way the brittleness-cap paragraph does, and have `rk check` (or a future
`rk audit`) read the live value from config rather than trusting whatever
number is written in HANDOFF.md's prose.
